items.note: It answers the question directly. The pattern is consistent with the increase driving Pro churn, but the data can't prove price caused it. The figures check out: Pro went from 1/39 to 10/50 and Basic from 1/40 to 3/53.
It removes all 15 trial accounts. 60 rows become 40, and the counts that follow are correct.
It removes all 5 @ourco.test accounts. These all cancelled in August, so leaving them in would have inflated Pro churn.
Churn is counted from cancel_month: 11 Pro and 4 Basic cancellations, which matches the data.

The writing is too technical and detailed for a CEO. It uses 'account-months at risk' and p-values, cites individual account IDs, and spends a long passage on how the price field is stored. It reads like an analyst memo, not an executive brief.

The section labelled 'Summary' has 5 bullets. But the full output is much longer: a confidence section with 6 top-level bullets and about 10 sub-bullets on assumptions, alternative explanations and next steps. That goes well past a summary of at most 5 bullets.
It suggests one specific chart: a monthly churn-rate line for Pro and Basic, with accounts at risk labelled and a vertical line at the July price change.
It rates confidence as low to moderate. It explains why: the Pro baseline rests on one cancellation, p is around a few percent, and one cancellation more or less would change the picture.
